basis: Albinism, intestinal aganglionosis and deafness define syndrome. Polycythemia in one infant lacks evidence of persistent blood dysfunction; fundus hypopigmentation alone is non-damaging.

decisions.haematologic: none: polycythemia in 1/1 is an isolated observation without evidence of persistent intrinsic blood disease or functional impairment.

basis: ATP synthase deficiency is metabolic; developmental impairment occurs in 3/6 and anemia in 2/3. Chronic diarrhea in 2/3 lacks evidence of direct intestinal injury or established enteropathy.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: chronic diarrhea in 2/3 establishes a common symptom but does not establish direct intestinal damage, malabsorption or enteropathy.

basis: Inner-ear endolymphatic sac epithelial tumor; destructive invasion of the petrous temporal bone occurs in most clinically apparent tumors (>50%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive petrous temporal bone invasion is characteristic and affects most clinically apparent tumors (>50%); this is direct tumor damage.

basis: Developmental impairment, hypotonia and epilepsy define this group of inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorders, which are inborn metabolic disorders. Other organ anomalies vary by subtype.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the group comprises inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis deficiencies, a class of congenital glycosylation and metabolic disorders.

basis: Malignancy of lymphatic vascular endothelium; most tumors (>50%) directly occupy skin and subcutis, commonly in chronically lymphedematous tissue. This is not lymphoma.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin and subcutis are the usual sites (>50%), with direct malignant occupation; the unspecified-site umbrella does not negate this common involvement.

basis: Developmental, cardiac and skeletal disease define syndrome; dermatitis 4/8 and cutis laxa 3/8 support skin involvement. Hepatic steatosis in one assessed case has uncertain prevalence.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermatitis occurs in 4/8 and cutis laxa in 3/8; the three primary slots prioritize defining neurologic, cardiac and skeletal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal anomalies are explicitly defining; scoliosis and delayed cranial suture closure are frequent (30-79%).

basis: Ear, eye and phalangeal defects occur in 80-99%; learning disability in 30-79%. Cleft palate (30-79%) omitted at cap; pigment changes lack damage; renal anomalies absent.

decisions.neurologic: involved: specific learning disability is part of the syndrome and occurs in 30-79%.
decisions.ocular: primary: strabismus is explicitly defining; strabismus and astigmatism are reported in 80-99%.
decisions.dermatologic: none: preauricular tags belong to the external ear; branchial remnants do not establish intrinsic skin disease, and pigment changes lack demonstrated damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining fifth-finger anomalies include phalangeal shortening and osteolytic defects, reported in 80-99%.

basis: Eye and skin anomalies define syndrome; genu varum and syndactyly occur in 80-99%, muscle atrophy in 30-79%. Thyroid abnormality (30-79%) lacks specified damage or dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: unspecified thyroid gland abnormality in 30-79% does not establish destructive pathology or endocrine dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal deformities and syndactyly occur in 80-99%, with muscle atrophy in 30-79%; these accompany the defining eye and skin phenotype.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration and dementia define disease; associated ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia in this neurodegenerative syndrome reflects impaired neurologic control of eye movement; intrinsic ocular disease is not established.

basis: Peripheral vascular syndrome with neuropathy annotated in 80-99%. Erythema is transient and ulcers occur in 5-29%; underlying blood disorders and diabetes are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: peripheral neuropathy is annotated in 80-99%, supporting common neural dysfunction within the neurovascular syndrome; the defining vascular axis remains primary.
